purpose: Test whether government-demand propagation and Federal Register public-inspection timing can be made historically point-in-time safe before any performance analysis.

candidates.name: GOVERNMENT_DEMAND_SHOCK_PROPAGATION × FROZEN_SUPPLIER_NETWORK
candidates.hypothesis: A newly disclosed federal contract award can convey an information shock about demand that may propagate to economically exposed suppliers or customers whose relationship map was frozen before the event.
candidates.construction: Use a fixed public population of newly recorded federal contract awards from USAspending. Define the award's authoritative observation boundary separately from its award/action date. Freeze issuer identity and the supplier/customer network from pre-event public information only. Exclude unresolved award modifications, retrospective data revisions and same-day ambiguous observation ordering.
sources: USAspending official API and data dictionary
SEC issuer identity and pre-event filings
public company filings for relationship-network freeze
candidates.next_gate: prove historical USAspending revision/public-observation boundary for a fixed sample; freeze award/action-state lineage; freeze issuer identity; build a pre-event-only relationship census; independently reproduce the event-time join

candidates.name: FEDERAL_REGISTER_PUBLIC_INSPECTION → PUBLICATION → EFFECTIVE_STAGE_GAP
candidates.hypothesis: For documents that are filed for public inspection before Federal Register publication, the official filing timestamp can define an earlier public-information boundary than publication; the lag to publication and effective date may contain an information-timing signal.
candidates.construction: Use Federal Register public-inspection records and the official filed-document timestamp as the earliest public boundary. Join the same document to its publication date and explicit effective date. Exclude documents without an authoritative filing time, special cases with ambiguous ordering, corrections that alter event identity, and any date selected after inspecting market outcomes.
sources: Office of the Federal Register public-inspection records
candidates.next_gate: historical public-inspection archive census; verify official filing timestamp extraction; map publication/effective dates; reconstruct correction/special-filing lineage; independently reproduce same-document joins
